item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q008_v1_atp_synthase_bulge_classification","answer":"The V1 ATP synthase A-subunit bulge domain shares the general β-sheet architecture of the barrel-sandwich-hybrid fold, but that structural resemblance does not establish homology with the fold’s other superfamilies. Its separate superfamily recognizes a distinct evolutionary group for which a common origin with those other groups is not supported by sufficiently convincing sequence or structural evidence.\n\nThe distinction is evolutionary: a family groups close homologues, a superfamily can unite more distant homologues, whereas a shared fold describes structural similarity without necessarily implying common ancestry. The all-β class is broader still. Separate superfamilies do not prove independent origins; very remote ancestry may remain unresolved.
